{"version":"2b1","blocks":[{"type":"text","text":"Decoupling a Conversation Engine, Context Engine, and Application Orchestrator involves clearly defining their responsibilities and interactions to ensure modularity and maintainability."},{"type":"text","text":"The Conversation Engine owns messages and lineage, managing the flow and history of the conversation. It should expose interfaces to receive input messages and provide output messages along with lineage metadata without depending on how context is selected or budgeted."},{"type":"text","text":"The Context Engine selects and budgets references, determining which contextual information to include and how much resource (e.g., token budget) to allocate. It should operate independently by receiving requests for context and returning selected references and budget details without managing message flow or orchestration."},{"type":"text","text":"The Application Orchestrator coordinates the Conversation and Context Engines, managing their interactions. It triggers context selection and budgeting from the Context Engine based on conversation state, then passes the selected context to the Conversation Engine to generate or process messages.
